content: The use of a pectoralis major muscle flap for onlay reinforcement may help reduce the risk of fistula formation following salvage total laryngectomy after concurrent chemoradiotherapy. However, the panels are unable to make a definitive recommendation either for or against the routine implementation of this procedure. For the management of the N0 neck during salvage surgery after non-surgical treatment, ipsilateral elective neck dissection is recommended in cases of recurrent supraglottic, transglottic, or rT3/rT4 glottic cancer. Bilateral elective neck dissection may be recommended for recurrent supraglottic cancer. Additionally, bilateral elective neck dissection can be considered in such cases, though this is not universally agreed upon. Elective neck dissection may be avoided in cases of recurrent glottic rT1N0 or rT2N0 cancer with an initial N0 status. In cases of recurrence after surgical therapy, extensive resection is recommended for eligible patients with stomal recurrence following total laryngectomy. Abbreviations used include: US (ultrasonography), MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), PFT (pulmonary function test), ABG (arterial blood gas), and ENT (ear, nose, and throat).
